reason: B-panel packing is the most direct test of input access and reuse, but its repeated packing cost and traversal changes make the outcome uncertain. Fusing A transpose with compute could reduce scratch traffic, though it repeats A loads across 16 column panels and has high register and correctness risk. The counter-width and ZA-order changes are small and source-expressible, with limited expected benefit; ZA reordering also risks tolerance. Scratch lifetime changes stack adjustments only, with no established performance opportunity. The two N=64 helper proposals are equivalent and both require an unavailable generated shape, so they rank last; test at most one if that helper becomes available.
